correctness.rationale: At dimension six the four listed centers are pairwise Hamming distance four, so their six-edge stars have disjoint endpoints and no cross adjacencies. Incident selected edges are compatible by triangle-freeness; disjoint edges conflict exactly at a one-bit cross adjacency. Automorphisms reduce exclusion of size 25 to a clique extension containing (0,1). In the checker, each color class is independent; after all later candidates have been tried and removed, the current prefix is colored by at most the color of its last vertex. Thus the early return when depth plus that color is below the target is sound. For every clique extension the branch of its last vertex preserves all earlier members by exact adjacency intersection. Candidate counts and all operations are exact. A separate bounded implementation, /workspace/branches/35c02605-dcf6-44ac-a1f7-8159d8284723/independent_eop_check.py, was run after a Q2 probe; its q6_replay.txt confirms 192 edges, the witness of 24, and exclusion of 25 after 54,111 calls. The original Q5 equality and induced-matching comparisons also reproduced; their removal is not a mathematical rejection. The submitted script was inspected, not executed. The repaired proof certifies this finite instance only and does not classify optimizers.

value.rationale: The binary hypercube and this packing invariant are studied explicitly in a product-graph comparison, with an exact theorem at power-of-two dimensions and a published finite-dimensional lower-bound table at other dimensions. At six the accessible bounds allowed anything from 24 to 32. Proving that 24 is sharp, rather than replacing an older witness by a larger one or picking an arbitrary family slice, fills that precise gap and gives a reliable benchmark for structural bounds and computations on the same invariant. The repaired claim makes no generalization from the finite result.
